mentions.section: Long the chips, short the returns
mentions.excerpt: Stephen Clapham, relaying Boston Partners’ analysis in The $4.4 Trillion Question, takes the issue to its terminal form: whether AI data-center economics ever earn an adequate return for anyone, Nvidia included.
Stephen Clapham of Behind the Balance Sheet asked in a June 7 analysis why Musk is listing now.
Stephen Clapham sees Kirby selling primary power rather than backup.
Stephen Clapham’s portfolio answer is close to zero exposure to Treasuries, except for long bonds issued at pandemic-era coupons that now trade near half their face value.
Stephen Clapham sees rising data-center costs, falling token prices and cheaper models, many of them Chinese, pressing on returns.
Stephen Clapham’s tank-terminal example makes the boundary vivid: land, permits, money and years are not a checkout feature.

sides.claim: Stephen Clapham states they would maintain a near-zero weight in US Treasuries, other than those trading at a near-50% discount to nominal value which they see as an asymmetric bet, a position they say they have covered in recent weeks.
